title: Spotting Scams and Phishing
drDigitalIntro:
Phishing is a fake message pretending to be someone you trust — your bank, a shop, a delivery company.

- The message wants you to click a link and hand over a password or card number.
- The words in a link can say anything. Only the address underneath it is real.
- Clicking a link to *look* at where it goes is safe. Typing your details into the page it opens is not.
- The tell is almost always the address: a strange ending, http:// instead of https://, or a familiar name spelled slightly wrong.
- Real companies never ask for a password by email. When in doubt, close the message and go to the site yourself.

playgroundTask.goal: You identified safe and dangerous links

steps.say: Open the message from First National Bank Security.
Click the link in the message to reveal where it really goes — then mark it Dangerous.
Reveal its link. It goes to the real amazon.com — mark it Safe.
Reveal its link: deals-4u-cheap.xyz over http. Mark it Dangerous.

drDigitalSuccess: You read three real messages and judged each one by its address rather than its wording. That is the whole skill — and it works in email, texts, and chat apps alike.
drDigitalHint: Click a message on the left to read it. The blue link inside is clickable — clicking it only reveals the address, it does not open the page. Then decide.
